title: Scope guard revert for out-of-scope files

parsed.summary: Scope auto-revert is not ready: tests fail, runtime-protected files are not reverted, and the new revert logic regresses flows that rely on generated out-of-scope assets.
issues: Scope is not clean: coder changed out-of-scope file tests/test_integration.py in addition to target files ralph.sh and src/ralph/resources/ralph.sh.

Acceptance is not met: the task requires runtime files (tasks.json, progress.md, .ralph/) to always be reverted, but the new Python filter and auto_revert_out_of_scope_files explicitly skip runtime-protected paths instead of reverting them.

Regression is present: the new worktree-wide revert deletes non-target files needed by existing flows, causing failures such as test_ralph_waits_for_assets_and_resumes_when_files_arrive where src/assets/hero-image.txt disappears before the test can read it.
Tests are not passing: 18 integration tests fail, including the newly added phase-mode scope test.
parsed.fix_instructions: Adjust the scope-guard implementation in ralph.sh and src/ralph/resources/ralph.sh so that, before lead review, it reverts runtime-protected paths as required and only auto-reverts true out-of-scope mutations without deleting legitimate generated assets needed by existing task/test flows; then rerun the integration suite until it passes.
